title: A brand's guide to TikTok Shop affiliate marketing
summary: TikTok Shop affiliate marketing works differently than other channels. Here's how to set commission rates, find the right creators, and build a program that compounds.
body_markdown:
TikTok Shop affiliate marketing is a commission-based program where creators promote a seller's products in videos, LIVEs and links, and earn a cut of every sale those posts drive. Sellers pay only when a sale happens. Creators get paid for the products they already like talking about.


Both sides use the same system inside TikTok. A shopper sees a product in a creator's video, taps it and buys without leaving the app. TikTok tracks the order, credits the creator and handles the commission.


This guide covers how the program works, how brands set up and grow an affiliate program, how creators join and start earning, and the mistakes that hold each side back.


## What is TikTok Shop affiliate marketing?


TikTok Shop affiliate marketing connects sellers who list products on TikTok Shop with creators who promote them. The seller sets a commission rate. The creator adds the product to their content. When a viewer buys, the creator earns that commission on the sale.


TikTok describes the program as "connecting creators and sellers through creativity and commission." For a brand, it's a pay-for-performance sales channel. For a creator, it's a way to earn from content without holding inventory or shipping anything.


### TikTok affiliate marketing vs TikTok Shop affiliate marketing


The two terms get used interchangeably, and they describe different setups.


General TikTok affiliate marketing means a creator promotes a product and sends viewers off TikTok through a link in their bio or a discount code. The sale happens on another site, and tracking depends on that site's affiliate program.


TikTok Shop affiliate marketing keeps the whole journey inside TikTok. The product is tagged in the video or LIVE, checkout happens in the app, and TikTok attributes the sale and pays the commission. For brands, that means cleaner attribution. For creators, it means one place to find products, post and get paid.


## How the TikTok Shop affiliate program works


Every affiliate sale follows the same loop.


1. The seller lists products and sets a commission. Sellers open an affiliate plan in TikTok Shop Seller Center and choose which products creators can promote and at what rate.
2. The creator picks products to promote. Creators browse available products, add the ones that fit their audience to their showcase and request samples where offered.
3. The creator posts shoppable content. According to TikTok Seller University, "Commissions are earned from orders via your shoppable videos, LIVEs, or sharable affiliate links."
4. A viewer buys inside TikTok. The product link in the post takes the shopper straight to checkout.
5. TikTok pays the commission. Creators are paid after the order is delivered and the after-sales period ends.


## For brands: how to run a TikTok Shop affiliate program


Getting started takes a few minutes. TikTok's steps are: "Log in to TikTok Shop Seller Center," then "Go to "Affiliate" > "Get Started" in the left-hand menu," then "Set up collaborations to reach more customers." The work that decides results comes after setup.


### Choose your collaboration type


TikTok Shop gives sellers two main ways to work with affiliates.


- Open collaboration lets any eligible creator find and promote your products. In TikTok's words, it lets "all affiliate creators discover and promote your products." It's the fastest way to build reach.
- Target collaboration lets you invite specific creators to promote specific products, usually at a different rate. TikTok describes it as working "with specific creators that fit your brand."


Most brands run both. Open collaboration brings in volume and helps you discover creators who already convert. Target collaboration is where you put a higher rate and closer attention on the creators who matter most. If a product sits in both, the target rate applies to the invited creator.


### Setting your commission rate


Commission is the main lever you control, and it shapes which creators pick up your products.


Category norms matter. Creators compare rates across similar products. If yours sits well below the category, the best creators will promote someone else.


Factor in your margins. Work out the rate you can afford after platform fees, sample costs and cost of goods. Pick a rate that wins creators and still leaves profit on every order.


You can tier it. Use a standard open rate for everyone and higher target rates for proven creators or the ones you're actively recruiting.


Ads-supported orders can carry their own rate. Some sellers can set a separate commission for orders driven by Shop Ads that run on a creator's content. TikTok's ads help center says, "You can set a commission rate from 1% and 80%," and notes, "This feature is only available to invited sellers." If you have access, it's a way to reward creators whose posts you're putting paid spend behind.


### Finding and working with the right creators


Waiting for creators to find you is slow. Brands that grow affiliate sales fastest recruit actively.


Look past follower count. Smaller creators with an engaged audience in your niche can outsell large accounts with a broad, general following. Look at a creator's recent shoppable posts, the products they already promote and how their audience responds.


Send samples **.** Creators sell what they've used. A sample lets them make honest, specific content, which is what converts on TikTok. Sellers set up samples inside the affiliate tools and approve or decline each request.


Give them a brief and let them write. Share the product's key benefits, what makes it different and anything they must or mustn't say. Then let the creator speak in their own voice. Their audience follows them for the way they talk.


Communicate clearly on rates and terms. Spell out the commission, how long it runs and any exclusivity before a creator starts posting. Clear terms prevent the disputes that end good partnerships.


### Affiliate platforms, agencies and MCNs


As a program grows, managing creators one at a time inside Seller Center gets hard. Three kinds of partner help.


- Affiliate and creator platforms help you discover creators, send outreach, manage samples and track results across hundreds of relationships.
- Agencies run the program for you, from recruiting and briefing creators to managing rates and reporting.
- MCNs (multi-channel networks) manage rosters of creators and can connect your products with many of them at once.


Smaller DTC brands often start with a platform and run the program in-house. Larger catalogs and brands selling across several marketplaces tend to bring in a partner that can manage creators, content, ads and the shop together.


### Organic affiliate content vs paid amplification


Organic creator content can sell on its own, and the best posts keep selling for weeks. Paid spend makes the winners go further.


The most efficient approach is to let organic content prove itself first. When a creator's video starts converting, boost it with Spark Ads, TikTok's format for running an existing post as an ad. You're putting budget behind content that already works, in the creator's own voice.


### What to track


Conversion rate by creator. Track which creators turn views into orders, and put your target rates and samples behind them.


GMV concentration. If one or two creators drive most of your sales, your program is fragile. Keep recruiting so no single creator can take your revenue with them.


Content type performance. Compare short videos with LIVEs, and reviews with tutorials or unboxings. Use what you learn in the next round of briefs.


## For creators: how to become a TikTok Shop affiliate


Creators can join TikTok Shop affiliate without buying inventory or shipping products. You choose what to promote, post about it and earn commission on what sells.


### Requirements to join


For US creators, TikTok Seller University lists these requirements:


- You must be at least 18 years old.
- Must have at least 1,000 followers.


You'll also confirm your age and verify your identity. TikTok notes that "1 ID can be used to verify up to 5 TikTok Shop creator accounts." To be paid, you'll set up a commission account, which "requires your personal and tax information."


Requirements vary by country and TikTok updates them regularly. The US page cited here was last updated in October 2026.


### The Creator Pilot Program


New creators with fewer than 5,000 followers don't get full access straight away. TikTok says "you will begin a 30-day Creator Pilot Program* as a new TikTok Shop creator if you have fewer than 5,000 followers."


During the pilot, you can promote products from shops with strong performance ratings (TikTok lists "shop performance of at least 95%"), and you're "Not eligible to join campaigns." There are also limits on how many shoppable videos and LIVEs you can post. Check Seller University for the current limits, since they change.


To graduate, TikTok lists these criteria:


- Onboarded for at least 30 days.
- Reach a minimum of 5,000 followers.
- Maintaining a clean record with a minimum of 176 points
- Published ≥ 6 e-commerce videos (at least 8 seconds)
- ≥ 1 E-commerce LIVE (at least 5 minutes)
- ≥ 10 orders in your e-commerce content (excluding fake orders) in the past 30 days
- Pass the Pilot Program Quiz.


Treat the pilot as practice. Use it to learn which products and formats your audience buys, so you graduate with a track record brands can see.


### How to apply


Once you meet the requirements, you'll register for TikTok Shop as a creator through the TikTok app and complete age and identity verification. After approval, you can browse products, add them to your showcase and start posting shoppable content.


### Finding products and brands to promote


Promote products you'd use anyway. Your audience can tell when a recommendation is real, and real recommendations convert.


Check each product's commission and the shop's ratings before you commit. TikTok shows the estimated commission when you choose a product: "you may check the estimated commission amount on the product detail page when you select from the product list." When a brand invites you to a target collaboration, compare the rate and terms with what's on offer through open collaboration.


### How commissions and payouts work


You earn commission on orders placed through your shoppable videos, LIVEs and affiliate links. The rate is set by the seller for each product, and it can differ between an open plan and a target collaboration you've been invited to.


Commission is paid after the order is delivered and the after-sales period ends. If the shopper returns the product before then, the commission on that order is cancelled.


### Tracking your earnings


Track which posts drive orders, which products convert best and how much you've earned from each. TikTok's creator tools show orders and commission for your shoppable content.


Look past total earnings. A product that earns a high rate on a few orders can be worth less than a lower rate that sells every day. The brands you work with are tracking the same numbers, so creators who know their conversion rate are easier to invite into target collaborations.


## Common mistakes on TikTok Shop affiliate


### Mistakes brands make


Setting it and forgetting it. An open plan left running with no recruiting, no samples and no rate reviews slowly fills with inactive creators. Treat the program as a channel someone owns.


Ignoring product page quality. A creator can send a shopper to your product, but a weak title, thin images or few reviews will lose the sale. Fix the product page before you scale creators.


Only working with large creators. Big accounts are expensive to win and don't always convert. A broad base of smaller, engaged creators is steadier and easier to grow.


Skipping the sample program. Without samples, creators either pass on your product or make generic content about something they haven't used.


### Mistakes creators make


Promoting everything. Posting about every product with a high rate erodes trust. Your audience buys because they believe you.


Ignoring the rules. Violations can cost you access to campaigns and pause your progress through the pilot. Read TikTok's content and shoppable video rules before you post.


Chasing rate over fit. A high commission on a product your audience doesn't want earns nothing. Pick products that suit your followers first.


Not tracking results. Without knowing which posts convert, you can't show brands your value or improve your own content.


## Keeping up with program changes


TikTok updates the affiliate program often, from creator requirements and pilot rules to commission tools and sample policies. The creator requirements cited in this guide were updated in October 2026. Before you change your rates, apply as a creator or plan a campaign, check TikTok Shop Seller University for the latest version of each rule.


## TikTok Shop affiliate marketing FAQ


### How does the TikTok Shop affiliate program work?


Sellers list products and set a commission rate in Seller Center. Creators add those products to their content. When a viewer buys through a creator's video, LIVE or affiliate link, TikTok tracks the sale and pays the creator their commission.


### How many followers do you need to be a TikTok Shop affiliate?


In the US, TikTok requires creators to be at least 18 and have at least 1,000 followers. Creators with fewer than 5,000 followers start in a 30-day Creator Pilot Program with some limits.


### What's the difference between open and target collaboration?


Open collaboration lets any eligible creator promote your products at your open rate. Target collaboration lets you invite specific creators, usually at a higher rate, to promote selected products.


### How do TikTok Shop affiliates get paid?


Creators earn commission on orders from their shoppable videos, LIVEs and affiliate links. Commission is paid after the order is delivered and the after-sales period ends, into a commission account set up with personal and tax information.


### How much commission should brands offer on TikTok Shop?


Start from your category's typical rates and your margin after fees, samples and cost of goods. Use a standard open rate, then offer higher target rates to proven creators.
